title: The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.5.
desc: The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.5. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know or discover an existing campaign and team ID to modify the team's name, story, goal, access and notification settings, set its profile image URL, and upload WordPress-allowed media files as parentless attachments. This vulnerability can be combined with CVE-2026-82568 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.

title: The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'sort' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.3 due to insufficient…
desc: The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'sort' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.3 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Successful exploitation requires the existence of at least one Peer-to-Peer campaign. This vulnerability can be combined with CVE-2026-82663 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.

title: Several endpoints that work on both issues and pull requests did not check which of the two the addressed item is.
desc: Several endpoints that work on both issues and pull requests did not check which of the two the addressed item is. A user who can read a repository's issues but not its pull requests could read pull request data through the issue sub-resources of the API (timeline, attachments, labels, subscriptions, tracked times and reactions), and list pull requests through the repository's issue search and milestone pages; the same applied in the other direction. These endpoints now check read access to the unit the item belongs to. The API endpoints were fixed in 28.2.0 and 28.3.0, the search and milestone pages in 28.4.0.

title: littlefs through 2.11.3, when built with LFS_MIGRATE, contains a type confusion vulnerability in lfs_dir_traverse() that treats a stack lfs_diskoff struct as an lfs_attr array.
desc: littlefs through 2.11.3, when built with LFS_MIGRATE, contains a type confusion vulnerability in lfs_dir_traverse() that treats a stack lfs_diskoff struct as an lfs_attr array. Attackers can supply a crafted littlefs v1 image whose metadata is read as LFS_FROM_USERATTRS during migration, causing out-of-bounds stack reads and process crashes.

title: Kroki before 0.36.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the BlockDiag family of engines that allows unauthenticated attackers to make server requests via node…
desc: Kroki before 0.36.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the BlockDiag family of engines that allows unauthenticated attackers to make server requests via node icon and background attributes. Attackers can send crafted diagrams to POST /blockdiag/svg or sibling endpoints to query internal services or cloud metadata and read local image files from the server.

title: Kroki before 0.36.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts via unvalidated svg-color-dark-scheme and…
desc: Kroki before 0.36.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts via unvalidated svg-color-dark-scheme and svg-color-light-scheme options. Attackers can craft a GET /goat/svg URL whose option value closes the SVG style element, executing JavaScript in the Kroki origin when victims open it.

title: Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SRP server mechanism because srp_server_mech_step2 does not reject client public values A that…
desc: Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SRP server mechanism because srp_server_mech_step2 does not reject client public values A that are multiples of N. Unauthenticated network clients can send A equal to N to force a zero shared secret, authenticating as any existing user without the password and learning session keys.

title: OkHttp through 5.5.1 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in CertificatePinner that skips pin checks because Pin.matchesHostname does not normalize…
desc: OkHttp through 5.5.1 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in CertificatePinner that skips pin checks because Pin.matchesHostname does not normalize trailing-dot hostnames. Network attackers with a CA-trusted certificate not matching configured pins can intercept or modify TLS traffic when applications request the trailing-dot form of pinned hosts.

title: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in MD2Importer::InternReadFile that allows attackers to read past the file buffer via an unvalidated stored…
desc: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in MD2Importer::InternReadFile that allows attackers to read past the file buffer via an unvalidated stored frameSize header field. Attackers can supply a crafted .md2 file loaded with a non-zero keyframe selected to crash the application or leak adjacent heap memory into the imported mesh.

title: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in OgreBinarySerializer::ReadSubMesh that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying crafted Ogre binary…
desc: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in OgreBinarySerializer::ReadSubMesh that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying crafted Ogre binary .mesh files. Attackers can set a large index count so the 32-bit buffer size wraps, causing a segmentation fault in aiMesh::~aiMesh() during scene teardown.

title: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in glTFCommon::Util::ParseDataURI caused by storing the data offset in a signed char.
desc: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in glTFCommon::Util::ParseDataURI caused by storing the data offset in a signed char. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF file with a raw data URI whose segment starts beyond byte 127 to crash applications or leak adjacent heap memory.

title: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the glTF and glTF2 importers that allows attackers to read local files via crafted buffers[].uri values.
desc: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the glTF and glTF2 importers that allows attackers to read local files via crafted buffers[].uri values. Attackers can supply glTF models with '..' segments or absolute paths in buffer URIs to load files like /etc/passwd into imported mesh vertex data.

title: Course-tencent-cloud before 2.0.2 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to view other users' refund previews by…
desc: Course-tencent-cloud before 2.0.2 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to view other users' refund previews by supplying an order sn to /api/refund/confirm. Attackers can compute valid sn values from Sqids-encoded sequential order ids using the default key to disclose ordered items, prices, refund amounts, fees and deadlines.

title: Netcccyun dnsmgr 2.18 before 2.22 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in POST /cloudflare/get_domain_default_line that allows restricted users to access domains…
desc: Netcccyun dnsmgr 2.18 before 2.22 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in POST /cloudflare/get_domain_default_line that allows restricted users to access domains outside their permissions. Restricted sub-users or single-domain logins can iterate the domain_id parameter to enumerate panel domain ids and read each domain's DNS line list and default line.

title: GeoPulse 1.5.0 through 2.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /api/v1/places/geocoding/{id} that allows authenticated users to read other users'…
desc: GeoPulse 1.5.0 through 2.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /api/v1/places/geocoding/{id} that allows authenticated users to read other users' private locations. Attackers can enumerate sequential reverse_geocoding_location ids to retrieve other users' custom place names, city, country, coordinates and bounding boxes from their history.

title: Zr.Admin.NET commit 1845017 through commit eb9228a contains a missing authorization vulnerability in TasksController.Get that allows any logged-in user to read scheduled task…
desc: Zr.Admin.NET commit 1845017 through commit eb9228a contains a missing authorization vulnerability in TasksController.Get that allows any logged-in user to read scheduled task details without the monitor:job permission. Attackers can obtain task ids from the unprotected /monitor/jobLog/list endpoint and retrieve job parameters, API URLs, cron expressions, and stored SQL statements.

title: Zr.Admin.NET commit af07ffc through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in SysProfileController.UpdateProfile that allows any authenticated…
desc: Zr.Admin.NET commit af07ffc through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in SysProfileController.UpdateProfile that allows any authenticated user to modify other accounts via UserId. Attackers can set the administrator's phone number to one they control, request an SMS code via /checkMobile, and log in through /PhoneLogin to take over the administrator account.

title: Zr.Admin.NET commit 0ee1ab8 through commit eb9228a contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows any logged-in user to read arbitrary server files via the path parameter of…
desc: Zr.Admin.NET commit 0ee1ab8 through commit eb9228a contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows any logged-in user to read arbitrary server files via the path parameter of /common/DownloadFile. Attackers can supply absolute paths or ../ sequences to read appsettings files and use the JwtSettings SecretKey to forge administrator tokens.

title: Zr.Admin.NET commit e6ceaf4 through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in FrontArticleController that allows authenticated users to change…
desc: Zr.Admin.NET commit e6ceaf4 through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in FrontArticleController that allows authenticated users to change other users' article visibility and pin state. Attackers can send PUT /front/article/changePublic with their own UserId in the body to make private articles public, then read them anonymously via GET /front/article/{id}.

title: Zr.Admin.NET commit 85cff6a through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /workflow/instance/{instanceId} that lets logged-in users…
desc: Zr.Admin.NET commit 85cff6a through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /workflow/instance/{instanceId} that lets logged-in users view others' workflow instances. Authenticated low-privilege attackers can enumerate sequential instance IDs to read other users' approval requests, including submitted form contents, applicant details and approval records.

title: When authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm, after a user logs in successfully once, subsequent logins for that user succeed with any password.
desc:
When authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm, after a user logs in successfully once, subsequent logins for that user succeed with any password.
A cached authentication skips the LDAP bind, and the AllowAllCredentialsMatcher installed by default in DefaultLdapRealm accepts any credentials, allowing an attacker who knows a valid username to authenticate as that user.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0, only when using DefaultLdapRealm (or JndiLdapRealm) with authenticationCachingEnabled set to true, which is not the default.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.1 or later, which fixes the issue by no longer installing AllowAllCredentialsMatcher by default.
Alternatively, disable authentication caching on the LDAP realm (this is the default), or configure a credentials matcher, such as SimpleCredentialsMatcher, that verifies credentials against the cached authentication info.

title: The web endpoint that removes an attachment skipped the permission check when the request came from the user who had uploaded the attachment, and it was reachable with read…
desc: The web endpoint that removes an attachment skipped the permission check when the request came from the user who had uploaded the attachment, and it was reachable with read access to issues or pull requests. A user who had uploaded a release asset could still delete it after losing write access to the repository. The endpoint now only deletes attachments that the user uploaded and that are not yet linked to an issue, comment or release.

title: Git over HTTP lowers the required permission for pushes to read access, so that the AGit flow works, and relies on the repository's server-side hooks to enforce write access.
desc: Git over HTTP lowers the required permission for pushes to read access, so that the AGit flow works, and relies on the repository's server-side hooks to enforce write access. A repository that is still being created by a migration, fork or template generation has no hooks yet, so a user with read access to it could push branches and tags during that window, or after a failed migration that left the repository in that state. Git over HTTP now refuses requests to repositories that are still being created.

title: Removing a team's review request looked up a review by the negated team ID, which for the team with ID 2 is the ID of the built-in Actions user, and marked the review it found as…
desc: Removing a team's review request looked up a review by the negated team ID, which for the team with ID 2 is the ID of the built-in Actions user, and marked the review it found as official. In the organization that owns that team, a user who can change the review requests of a pull request could make an approval left by the Actions user count toward the approvals required by branch protection. Merging still required permission to merge. Removing a team review request no longer changes any review.

title: When Gitea acts as an OAuth2 or OpenID Connect provider, the token endpoint did not check the state of the user.
desc: When Gitea acts as an OAuth2 or OpenID Connect provider, the token endpoint did not check the state of the user. After an administrator deactivated an account or prohibited its sign-in, existing refresh tokens and unused authorization codes of that user could still be exchanged for new tokens, so applications that sign users in through Gitea kept them signed in. The token endpoint now refuses users who may not sign in, and token introspection reports their tokens as inactive.

title: A pull request review created through the API as a draft (`event` set to `PENDING` or left empty) was added to the pull request timeline and announced through notifications and…
desc: A pull request review created through the API as a draft (`event` set to `PENDING` or left empty) was added to the pull request timeline and announced through notifications and activity feeds like a submitted review. Its body and line comments were therefore visible to everyone who can read the pull request, including anonymous visitors of a public repository, before the reviewer submitted it. Pending reviews no longer get a timeline entry or notifications until they are submitted.

title: The Custom Block Builder WordPress plugin before 3.0.0 does not properly deny unauthorised requests to its REST routes, as its permission checks return a non-error response that…
desc: The Custom Block Builder  WordPress plugin before 3.0.0 does not properly deny unauthorised requests to its REST routes, as its permission checks return a non-error response that WordPress treats as granted, allowing unauthenticated users to execute arbitrary PHP code on the server.

title: Replying to a code review comment accepted a review ID that belongs to a different pull request, through the web form, the API and incoming mail replies.
desc: Replying to a code review comment accepted a review ID that belongs to a different pull request, through the web form, the API and incoming mail replies. A signed-in user could reply on a pull request they can access with the ID of a review in a repository they cannot read, and the new comment was attached to that review and received the diff context of the commented lines. Replies are now only accepted for a review of the same pull request, and for a pending review only from its author.

desc: `GET /api/v1/users/{username}/orgs/{org}/permissions` only checked that the organization is visible to the caller and then returned the named user's role in it. Any signed-in user could learn whether another user is an owner, admin or member of a public or limited organization, including for members who conceal their membership. The roles are now only returned to the user themselves, to members of the organization and to site administrators.

title: A repository created with auto-init accepted pushes before its initialization had finished, and the initial commit was built in a checkout of whatever the repository already…
desc: A repository created with auto-init accepted pushes before its initialization had finished, and the initial commit was built in a checkout of whatever the repository already contained. A user who is allowed to create repositories could push a crafted tree during that window so that writing the README followed a symbolic link and overwrote a server-side git hook, which runs commands as the Gitea system user. The initial commit is now built in a freshly initialized directory, and a new repository only becomes ready, and accepts pushes, once its initialization is complete.

desc: The Burst Statistics  WordPress plugin before 3.7.5 does not enforce a shared report's date range on the analytics it serves to the report's share link, allowing anyone holding the link to read the report's statistics for any period the site retains rather than the period the report was shared for.

desc: The WPGraphQL WordPress plugin before 2.27.1 does not restrict access to posts in custom non-public post statuses, allowing users with the Contributor role and above to read the content of other users' posts in those statuses.

title: The AGit flow (pushing to `refs/for/...`) did not check the pusher's access to pull requests again when it created the pull request.
desc: The AGit flow (pushing to `refs/for/...`) did not check the pusher's access to pull requests again when it created the pull request. A user or deploy key with read access to the code only, or with write access to the wiki over SSH, could open pull requests in a repository where they have no access to pull requests. Creating a pull request through AGit now requires read access to the pull requests of the repository and is refused for wiki pushes.

title: The "Protected file patterns" setting of a branch protection rule was checked against file names as git prints them, and git quotes names that contain a double quote, a backslash…
desc: The "Protected file patterns" setting of a branch protection rule was checked against file names as git prints them, and git quotes names that contain a double quote, a backslash or a control character. Such names never matched a pattern, so a user with write access could add or change files under a protected pattern by direct push or through a pull request merge, and could move a protected file out of the pattern's reach by renaming it. Where the patterns protect workflow files, this allowed adding a workflow that then ran on the repository's runners. Changed files are now listed unquoted, and a rename reports both the old and the new path.

title: When a release was edited, the files of the attachments to remove were deleted by the identifiers submitted in the form rather than by the attachments verified to belong to the…
desc: When a release was edited, the files of the attachments to remove were deleted by the identifiers submitted in the form rather than by the attachments verified to belong to the release. A user with write access to the releases of any repository, including their own, could submit a crafted identifier that resolves to the stored file of another attachment and delete it, provided they know that attachment's UUID. The attachment record stayed, so downloads of the affected issue, comment or release file failed. Release edits now only delete the files of attachments that belong to the release.

title: When a file is edited in a fork through the web editor, Gitea can first copy a branch from the base repository into the fork.
desc: When a file is edited in a fork through the web editor, Gitea can first copy a branch from the base repository into the fork. That copy did not check whether the user may read the base repository's code. A user who had forked a repository and later lost access to it, for example after it was made private or they were removed as a collaborator, could keep copying its current branches into their fork and read them. The copy now requires read access to the code of the base repository.

title: The repository search used by the dashboard (`GET /repo/search`) returned the internal commit status object of each repository.
desc: The repository search used by the dashboard (`GET /repo/search`) returned the internal commit status object of each repository. Since 28.0.0 that object included the repository owner's full user record, so any signed-in user could read the password hash, salt and email address of the owner of any repository they can see that has a commit status. The response now contains only the state and target URL of the commit status.

title: Gitea accepted an unlimited number of wrong TOTP passcodes during sign-in, in the password reset flow and for Basic authentication with the `X-Gitea-OTP` header.
desc: Gitea accepted an unlimited number of wrong TOTP passcodes during sign-in, in the password reset flow and for Basic authentication with the `X-Gitea-OTP` header. An attacker who already knows an account's password could guess the six-digit passcode by trying codes at a high rate and sign in despite two-factor authentication. After five failed passcodes, further attempts for the account are now refused for 15 minutes.

title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Barn2 Plugins Document Library Pro document-library-pro allows Object Injection.This issue affects Document Library Pro: from…
desc: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Barn2 Plugins Document Library Pro document-library-pro allows Object Injection.This issue affects Document Library Pro: from n/a before 4.2.2.

title: When a container blob upload was rejected, for example because it exceeded a package size quota, the cleanup removed the blob from storage even if the same content already…
desc: When a container blob upload was rejected, for example because it exceeded a package size quota, the cleanup removed the blob from storage even if the same content already existed and was used by other packages. On an instance with a package quota configured, a user who can upload container images and has the exact content of another owner's package file or image layer could make it undownloadable. The cleanup now only removes blobs that the failed upload created.

title: The popup shown when hovering an issue reference loaded its data from the path of the hovered link and inserted part of the response as HTML.
desc: The popup shown when hovering an issue reference loaded its data from the path of the hovered link and inserted part of the response as HTML. A user who can post a comment or other rendered content could add a link that is displayed as an ordinary issue reference but points to a file in a repository they control, so that the popup inserted that file's content into the page of anyone hovering the link and ran script in the viewer's session. The popup now requests the issue by the owner, repository and index parsed from the link.

title: With `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = true`, the Git LFS endpoints still answered unauthenticated requests for repositories that are not private.
desc: With `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = true`, the Git LFS endpoints still answered unauthenticated requests for repositories that are not private. An anonymous client who knows the path of such a repository and the SHA-256 of an LFS object could download the object, and could use the batch endpoint to test whether an object exists. The Git LFS endpoints now require authentication when sign-in is required to view the instance.

title: A repository registered by its owner as a source of scoped workflows kept that registration when it was transferred to another owner.
desc: A repository registered by its owner as a source of scoped workflows kept that registration when it was transferred to another owner. The new owner could then change the workflows in the transferred repository, and they kept running in the previous owner's repositories with access to their Actions secrets and job tokens. A transfer now removes the owner-level registrations of the repository, and registrations whose source repository no longer belongs to the registering owner are ignored.

title: The RubyGems package registry accepted gems whose platform, dependency names or dependency version requirements contain newline characters.
desc: The RubyGems package registry accepted gems whose platform, dependency names or dependency version requirements contain newline characters. Because the compact index served to clients is line-based, a user who can publish a gem to an owner's registry could forge index entries, such as packages that do not exist or additional versions of an existing gem with dependencies of their choice. Clients that resolve gems from that registry could then be led to install attacker-chosen dependencies. Gems with such metadata are now rejected.

title: The A2Reviews WordPress plugin through 1.2.3 does not properly verify authorization on several of its API command handlers, relying on a signature keyed on a value that is empty…
desc: The A2Reviews WordPress plugin through 1.2.3 does not properly verify authorization on several of its API command handlers, relying on a signature keyed on a value that is empty by default on an unconnected install, allowing unauthenticated attackers to modify A2Reviews WordPress plugin through 1.2.3 settings and product review metadata and to read non-public product metadata.

title: The Membership Plugin WordPress plugin before 4.0.6 does not verify that the membership referenced in a saved-card payment request belongs to the user making it, allowing…
desc: The Membership Plugin  WordPress plugin before 4.0.6 does not verify that the membership referenced in a saved-card payment request belongs to the user making it, allowing subscriber-level members to disclose another member's Stripe payment client secret and attach a payment method of their choosing to another member's pending payment.

title: The Membership Plugin WordPress plugin before 4.0.6 does not perform any authorization or CSRF check before running a schema-altering database maintenance routine, allowing…
desc: The Membership Plugin  WordPress plugin before 4.0.6 does not perform any authorization or CSRF check before running a schema-altering database maintenance routine, allowing unauthenticated users to convert the Membership Plugin  WordPress plugin before 4.0.6's own tables to a narrower character set, which irreversibly replaces every 4-byte character (such as emoji and some CJK characters) in the membership level, discount code and payment records with a question mark.

title: The RegistrationMagic WordPress plugin before 6.1.0.4 does not verify ownership of the submitted email address before updating the associated WordPress user account, allowing…
desc: The RegistrationMagic  WordPress plugin before 6.1.0.4 does not verify ownership of the submitted email address before updating the associated WordPress user account, allowing unauthenticated attackers to overwrite the profile fields of arbitrary non-administrator users by submitting a public form that contains name and primary-email fields.

title: The RegistrationMagic WordPress plugin before 6.1.0.4 does not properly escape a user-supplied value before printing it inside an inline script block on several of its admin…
desc: The RegistrationMagic  WordPress plugin before 6.1.0.4 does not properly escape a user-supplied value before printing it inside an inline script block on several of its admin screens, allowing unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the session of an administrator who is tricked into opening a crafted link.

title: The RegistrationMagic WordPress plugin before 6.1.0.4 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement, which could allow high privilege users such as…
desc: The RegistrationMagic  WordPress plugin before 6.1.0.4 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement, which could allow high privilege users such as admin to perform SQL injection attacks.

title: The Auth Armor WordPress plugin through 1.0.3 does not require authentication on several handlers available to logged-out users, which leak the site's stored API credentials and…
desc: The Auth Armor  WordPress plugin through 1.0.3 does not require authentication on several handlers available to logged-out users, which leak the site's stored API credentials and allow an unauthenticated attacker to reset an administrator's enrollment and take over that administrator account.

title: The Payment Gateway via Valitor for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 1.9.41 does not properly validate the authenticity of payment callbacks, relying on a verification secret…
desc: The Payment Gateway via Valitor for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 1.9.41 does not properly validate the authenticity of payment callbacks, relying on a verification secret that ships with a hard-coded default value used by every store that has not changed it, allowing unauthenticated attackers to forge a valid payment confirmation and mark arbitrary orders as paid.

title: MicroQuickJS (mquickjs) before commit 99eed3f contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability because JS_Call() raises exceptions during frame setup without updating ctx->sp and…
desc: MicroQuickJS (mquickjs) before commit 99eed3f contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability because JS_Call() raises exceptions during frame setup without updating ctx->sp and ctx->fp. Attackers can supply JavaScript that calls a non-function value, causing build_backtrace() to walk stale frame pointers and crash the engine for denial of service.

title: GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in ctxload_process() that passes non-object descriptors to ODS_SetupOD() without checking the descriptor tag.
desc: GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in ctxload_process() that passes non-object descriptors to ODS_SetupOD() without checking the descriptor tag. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file with a URL-bearing descriptor that crashes MP4Box or other GPAC-based applications in gf_scene_ns_connect_object(), causing denial of service.

title: GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_dash_group_get_audio_channels() in src/media_tools/dash_client.c that allows attackers to crash…
desc: GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_dash_group_get_audio_channels() in src/media_tools/dash_client.c that allows attackers to crash applications via crafted DASH manifests. Attackers can supply an MPD whose AudioChannelConfiguration element omits schemeIdUri or value, crashing MP4Box or GPAC DASH clients and causing denial of service.

title: GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_node_get_field_by_name() in src/scenegraph/base_scenegraph.c that lets attackers crash applications.
desc: GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_node_get_field_by_name() in src/scenegraph/base_scenegraph.c that lets attackers crash applications. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene referencing a never-created node to crash MP4Box or GPAC scene loader applications, causing denial of service.

title: GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in m2tsdmx_update_sdt() in src/filters/dmx_m2ts.c that allows attackers to crash the MPEG-2 TS demuxer.
desc: GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in m2tsdmx_update_sdt() in src/filters/dmx_m2ts.c that allows attackers to crash the MPEG-2 TS demuxer. Attackers can supply a crafted .ts file with an invalid service descriptor leaving service or provider names NULL to crash MP4Box and cause denial of service.
